body: Thanks for taking the time to submit an issue. Python [imports are case-sensitive](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0235/#current-lower-left-semantics) so I don't think there's anything to fix here.

@brycedrennan isn't the `import` statement case sensitive, but the package naming itself not case sensitive?  I think in this case Poetry should be case insensitive, but the application one might build with poetry would need to be case sensitive when actually using whatever dependencies Poetry is managing?

https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0508/#id21

Alternatively, if this is not a poetry bug, how would you recommend adding the development branch of Logbook as a dependency to a project managed by poetry?

Thanks!
Reopening till we answer your question.

issue.title: Use canonical name when validating package from directory

repository.name: poetry
repository.description: Python packaging and dependency management made easy

issue.body:
This change handles cases where a project uses a non-canonical name in its setup configuration (eg: [Logbook](https://github.com/getlogbook/logbook/blob/develop/setup.py#L188).

Incorrect behavior was introduced with c6a2d6e17772baf31fae4ece3f8b2449e2a36d97 where the comparison used the raw name value instead of the canonical name.

Closes: #1303 

### Pull Request Check List

- [x] Added **tests** for changed code.

## Issue

poetry does not seem to correctly handle packages with capital letters

``` bash

```
### Inspect pyproject. 
It correctly contains the capitalized name
``` shell
$ cat myPackage/pyproject.toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "myPackage"
version = "0.1.0"
description = ""
authors = ["Panos Mavrogiorgos <pmav99@gmail.com>"]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^2.7"

[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]
pytest = "^4.6"

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry>=0.12"]
build-backend = "poetry.masonry.api"
```
Nevertheless, the created package is in lowercase...
``` shell
$ ls myPackage
mypackage  tests  README.rst  pyproject.toml
```

$  poetry build

$ mv mypackage myPackage
$ ls

$ poetry build -vvv
/home/pmav99/.poetry/lib/poetry/_vendor/py2.7/subprocess32.py:149: RuntimeWarning: The _posixsubprocess module is not being used. Child process reliability may suffer if your program uses threads.

Traceback (most recent call last):

    return Application().run()

    self._render_traceback(io, tb)

    io.write_line("".join(traceback.format_list(frames)))
